text: {"lessons":["Selling Stock B and Stock E after gains shows how satisfying it can feel to lock in profits, but my average cost should not determine whether I keep a stock; I should assess its prospects and role in my portfolio.","I made no trades for most periods, and the account moved both up and down; I should not treat these short-term changes as a forecast or trade without a reason grounded in my plan.","I should resist judging each stock as a separate win-or-loss account: avoiding a painful loss or chasing the pleasure of a gain can distort decisions, so I should apply consistent standards to all holdings."]}
